before.body: На э́той у́лице есть францу́зы — There are Frenchmen on this street. В Москве́ есть ста́рые зда́ния — There are old buildings in Moscow.

after.title: Presence and the nominative
after.body: Use the presence construction when the line says that something exists. In these supplied examples, the noun naming what exists is nominative. Read the Russian line and identify whether it states presence. На э́той у́лице есть францу́зы — There are Frenchmen on this street. В Москве́ есть ста́рые зда́ния — There are old buildings in Moscow.

before.title: Admitted instruction
before.body: Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word

after.title: Absence and the genitive
after.body: Use the absence construction when the line says that something does not exist. In these supplied examples, the absence word is followed by a genitive noun. Presence and absence require different case explanations.

before.title: Admitted lines
before.body: Нет рестора́нов — There are no restaurants. В Москве́ нет ста́рых зда́ний — There are no old buildings in Moscow.

after.title: Compare the complete examples
after.body: Compare the positive and negative lines below. For a positive line choose the nominative presence explanation; for a negative line choose the genitive absence explanation. Нет рестора́нов — There are no restaurants. В Москве́ нет ста́рых зда́ний — There are no old buildings in Moscow.

В Москве́ есть ста́рые зда́ния — There are old buildings in Moscow.

before.title: Admitted lines
before.body: У меня есть Х — I have X. У вас есть сын? — Do you have a son?

after.title: The possessor and the possessed thing
after.body: In the simple possession pattern shown here, the possessor after the possession preposition is genitive. The thing possessed is nominative. The schematic slot in the first example represents that possessed thing. У меня есть Х — I have X. У вас есть сын? — Do you have a son?

before.title: Admitted instruction
before.body: The thing that is possessed remains in the nominative

after.title: Possession versus absence
after.body: A simple positive possession line places the possessed thing in the nominative. An absence line places the absent thing in the genitive. Decide whether the whole shown line affirms or denies possession.

before.title: Admitted lines
before.body: Да, у меня есть сын. — Yes, I have a son. У твоего́ му́жа есть оди́н друг — Your husband has one friend.

after.title: Positive statements and questions
after.body: The son examples keep the same simple possession pattern in a statement or question: genitive possessor and nominative possessed thing. The form of a question does not turn the noun into an absence construction. Да, у меня есть сын. — Yes, I have a son. У твоего́ му́жа есть оди́н друг — Your husband has one friend.

before.title: Admitted lines

after.title: Review the complete constructions
after.body:
In the simple possession pattern shown here, the possessor after the possession preposition is genitive. The thing possessed is nominative. The schematic slot in the first example represents that possessed thing. У меня есть Х — I have X. У вас есть сын? — Do you have a son? 

A simple positive possession line places the possessed thing in the nominative. An absence line places the absent thing in the genitive. Decide whether the whole shown line affirms or denies possession.

The son examples keep the same simple possession pattern in a statement or question: genitive possessor and nominative possessed thing. The form of a question does not turn the noun into an absence construction. Да, у меня есть сын. — Yes, I have a son. У твоего́ му́жа есть оди́н друг — Your husband has one friend. 

The many-friends example includes a quantity expression. Quantity patterns are separate from the simple nominative possessed thing in the son checks. The no-son example below denies possession and uses the genitive for the absent thing. У моего нового мужа есть много друзе́й — My new husband has many friends. У меня́ нет сы́на — No, I don't have a son. 

The no-money example also denies possession. Choose the genitive absence explanation, rather than the simple positive possession explanation. У моего́ бра́та нет де́нег — My brother doesn't have any money.
